description.narrative: ADB and the Government of Sri Lanka are working together to provide people in the country with the skills they need to get good jobs. The Skills Sector Enhancement Program is improving the teacher training and the government's overall quality assurance efforts in regards to technical training. It is also helping the Sri Lankan government analyze where the gaps are greatest in the labor market's demand for skills. This is allowing technical training to be focused on the areas where there is the most demand. The program is also working to increase the number of students enrolled in technical programs to 172,000 and is providing financial help to at least 18,000 students from disadvantaged situations. The program is working to improve coordination, monitor and evaluation of skills development efforts and strengthen performance management of publicly financed training initiatives.

description.narrative: Market-responsive and inclusive TVET system developed

62% of graduates (50% of female graduates) with NVQ employed 6 months after training completion (2011 baseline: 47.5%—male 55.8%, female 34.8%; 2015 update: 57%—male 64%, female 47%) (DLI 1) Achievement: 70.66 Progress/Status: According to the second tracer study conducted by CEPA the employment of NVQ graduates has been increased from 57.4 in 2016 to 70.66% in 2020 (female 61.38%). Data Source: Third-party validation through tracer study in 2016 and 2019
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: (I) At least nine university colleges established (2014 baseline: none) (PAP 1.5) Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: As of Sep 2022, 9 university colleges are established and in operation including 3 PPP mode university colleges.
Note- 1 PPP university college is not in operation currently. Data Source: MOU executed, SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report on the number of PPP universities

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: At least 15 training programs updated or developed based on the skills forecasting report (2017 baseline: none) (DLI 4) Achievement: 15 Progress/Status: -15 new/revised programmes have been implemented by IAs of SSDP since 2017. Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: At least 80% of NVQ 4-6-level program graduates completed on-the-job training (2014 baseline: not available) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All graduates of NVQ level 4-6 have undergone OJT (100%). Data Source: Student tracking system at TVEC and/or MSDVT

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: At least four ISSCs established to provide workforce planning services to industry groups and the government (2014 baseline: none) (PAP 1.6); Achievement: 4 Progress/Status: Four ISSCs have been established in four priority areas (ICT, Construction, Manufacturing & Engineering Services and Hospitality & Tourism). Data Source: SSDD ASPR on the new training programs introduced as per skills gap analysis or industry request

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: Skills forecasting report for at least six priority sectors developed; Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Skills forecasting reports were prepared for ICT, Construction, Manufacturing and Automobile sectors. Skills forecast for Tourism sector developed and validation to be done. Health sector report is being done. Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: i. At least two (2) through PPPs Achievement: 1 Data Source: MOU executed, SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report on the number of PPP universities

Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: (I) At least 35,000 existing workers assessed and certified through recognition of prior learning during 2014-2020 (2014 baseline: not applicable) (PAP 1.4) Achievement: 4663 Progress/Status: 59,356 existing industry workers were certified as of Sep 2022. Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: (I) At least 60,000 students from poor, disadvantaged groups received stipends to bridge critical skills gap during 2014-2020 (2014 baseline: not applicable) (PAP 1.7) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: DTET, VTA and CGTTI have provided scholarships and bursaries to 47,200 students between 2014-2016 and 28,811 from 2017-2020- Q3
Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report
Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: i. Female participation is to be at least 30% Achievement: 28 Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report
Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: i. Out of the 60,000 students female target is 30% Achievement: 30 Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: TVET sector management to implement policy, institutional, and operational reforms improved Indicator: Performance-based financing pilot-tested in at least 100 training centers by 2020 (2014 baseline: no centers) (DLI 7) Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: 138 centers have prepared Center Management Plans.
Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report and third-party validation

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: At least 4,000 private sector workers (cumulative) participated in skills-upgrading training aligned with NVQ (2016 baseline: none) (DLI 6) Achievement: 960 Progress/Status: As of Oct 2023, 3006 industry workers participated skills upgrading training aligned with NVQ. Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: (I) At least five new training programs conducted to improve employability (2016 baseline: none) (DLI 1, PAP 1.7) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 09 new programs were developed and implemented, 2051 students have been enrolled up to Dec 2020
Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report
Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: i. the above training programs target 1,300 women Achievement: 1193 Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: (I) At least 675 TVET graduates received SEPI loan during 2017-2020 (2017 baseline: not applicable) (DLI 1) Achievement: 7 Progress/Status: 325 NVQ graduates received SEPI loans in 2017 and 275 in 2018, 110 in 2019 and 170 in 2020, 7 in 2021. Total is 887.
Data Source: SEPI loan report from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka
Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: i. Of whom at least 50% are female Achievement: 70 Data Source: SEPI loan report from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka

Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: (I) At least 224,000 students enrolled in quality-assured TVET (2012 baseline: 148,131 students, of whom 45.3% are female) (DLI 6) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 250,690 students have enrolled as of Dec 2019.
Data Source: TVEC Labour Market Information Bulletin

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: At least 75% of instructors (cumulative) attended industry exposure training (2016 baseline: 25.7%) (DLI 3) Achievement: 94 Progress/Status: 2,683 instructors (94% of academic staff) have attended industry exposure training as of June 2022
Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report on human resource development and/or training records

Output: Improved quality of TVET provision Indicator: Vocational teacher vacancy ratio across seven implementing agencies maintained at less than 15% (March 2017 baseline: 32%) (DLI 3) Achievement: 12.5 Progress/Status: As of June 2022, vocational teacher vacancy ratio is 12.5%. Without DTET.
Data Source: SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report

Output: Industry partnership for TVET planning and provision enhanced Indicator: i. At least 20% of whom are women Achievement: 23 Data Source: Agreements executed, SSDD's Annual Sector Performance Report on the number of people trained
Output: TVET participation and equitable access increased Indicator: i. Female enrollment is 45% Achievement: 43 Data Source: TVEC Labour Market Information Bulletin

Output: TVET sector management to implement policy, institutional, and operational reforms improved Indicator: Significantly negative findings from sample-based procurement review reduced to less than 20% of reviewed contracts by 2019 (2015 baseline: 51%) (DLI 8, PAP 3.8) Achievement: 16.4 Progress/Status: As confirmed by AFR, critical findings of contracts were reduced to 16.4% by 2019. Data Source: Annual fiduciary review

Output: TVET sector management to implement policy, institutional, and operational reforms improved Indicator: At least 85% of the annual budget for the SSDP expended by 2020 (2013 baseline: 68.7% MSDVT spending rate) (PAP 2.3) Achievement: 98 Progress/Status: For 2020, 98% of annual recurrent budget and 84% capital budget spent. Data Source: MOF annual report (expenditure analysis section)
Output: Improved quality of TVET provision Indicator: i. Male graduates- 70.8 Achievement: 53 Data Source: Student tracking system at TVEC and/or MSDVT

Output: Improved quality of TVET provision Indicator: (I) 80% of TVET enrollees, both male and female, graduated (2012 baseline: 71.3%—male 70.8%, female 71.9%) Achievement: 60 Progress/Status: 2019, there were 70.23% of TVET enrollees graduated, however, due to closure of training centers in 2020 the ratios were reduced to 60% (total). In 2021 it was further dropped to 50%
The target was not achieved. The reason for this is that there are several new challenges we (the Sector) had to face that did not exist during the design phase of the program. The challenges are; making TVET education free of charge (This made the dropout higher by a significant amount). Easter Attack, the Covid lockdown, and the economic crisis at present. In 2021, to assess the reasons for Dropouts, a dropout survey was conducted by a selected consultant.
Their findings as the reasons for dropouts are 1. Go for employment 2. Financial difficulties 3. Following the wrong program 4. The program is too hard, not enough knowledge (like maths) 5. Transport difficulties 6. Go for higher Education etc.
for some of these reasons we have already established measures to minimize the effect Such as, 1. More Career Guidance at all levels (Grade 9, OL, AL, At the entrance to VTCs) 2. Introduction of the bursary scheme (Sisu Diriya) etc.
Data Source: Student tracking system at TVEC and/or MSDVT
Output: Improved quality of TVET provision Indicator: ii. Female graduates- 71.9 Achievement: 47 Data Source: Student tracking system at TVEC and/or MSDVT
